::: {#def-lambda}
#### `lambda`

The Racket expression

```racket
(lambda (x1 ... xn)
  body)
```

is a **`lambda` expression**.
Its value is the function with parameters `x1`, ..., `xn` whose value at its arguments is the value of `body`,
found as in @def-racket-define.
The function has no name.
The body may use any name defined where the `lambda` expression appears,
as the body of the `lambda` in `pair-with` (@exr-pair-with) uses `y`.

The definition `(define (f x) body)` is shorthand for `(define f (lambda (x) body))`:
it gives the name `f` to the function the `lambda` expression makes.

:::

*Video:* Jerry Cain uses `lambda` with `map` in Scheme, the language Racket grew out of, in [Stanford CS 107 Lecture 22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3LeCydausnk) [@cain2008cs107videos].
